about: Hand-labelled exploration moves (plan change CX1) for the router's recall test (packages/classical/test/moves.test.ts).

The statements: every 15th problem of bench/fc-bench-v1-discrete.json from index 7 (38 problems, picked by index, not by content), and the two Putnam statements the repository holds (PutnamBench itself is downloaded, not committed).

The labels say which moves a person would set a CPU tool on, from the statement alone: E1 the statement ranges over a class of finite structures; E2 it asks for an object (an ∃, a refutation of a ∀, the witness side of an extremal value); E3 a ∀ whose small instances can be checked (not an eventual statement); E4 the object is a sequence or a function of n; E5 an iteration or process; E6 a polynomial inequality, an integer equation or an arithmetic impossibility; E8 a parameter bounded to finitely many values; E9 a bound on, or the value of, an extremal quantity; E12 growth, limits or densities.

E7, E10 and E11 are never labelled: every proof may need them, and the syntax gives no signal for them. The labels were written before the rules were tuned and were not changed to fit them, except #22 (E9 added) and #517 (E3 dropped: an eventual statement has no finite counterexample), both for consistency with the definitions above.
